title: Polynomial-time clean emission
statement: For every polynomial-time computable function $f$ from Boolean words to Boolean words, there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $A,d$ such that $M$ has at least one work tape and, for every Boolean input word $x$ and argument word $z$, there is a positive time $t\le A(|z|+1)^d$ at which the run from the initial state with $z$ on the first work tape and all other work tapes blank first halts. At that time its configuration has $f(z)$ on the first work tape, all other work tapes blank, and output exactly $f(z)$; the input head and work-tape heads and contents are those of the canonical starting configuration, apart from the first tape now containing $f(z)$.
replaced:
For every polynomial-time computable word function $f$ there exist a module $M$
and constants $A, d$ such that $M$ satisfies the clean-module contract with the
identity as result function, emission $f$, and budget $n \mapsto A\,(n+1)^d$:
the emit-mode module preserves its argument and forwards the exact computed
chunk, with cleanup and the final halt inside the polynomial budget.
